thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: latency SLO breaches on prod cluster after canary shift. Auto-tags: feature=batching-opt, kernel=affinity-experimental. Dashboard: https://redwood.ai/observability/incident/zz01 :rotating_light:

alice oncall: Got the page. Noted start time ~10m ago. Who initiated the canary?

deploy-bot: Canary canary-2026 started by @frank infra at 1918009000. Traffic ramped 5% -> 20%. Config: kernel_affinity=experimental, batching=optimized.

bob runtime: I'm seeing p99 spikes and many hosts reporting kernel fallback events. Batching coordinator logs show frequent forced flushes. Example logs:
```
2026-03-15T15:02:01Z host-07 kernel-select: attempted affinity experimental -> fallback simd-compat (missing optimized kernel)
2026-03-15T15:02:01Z host-07 batch-coordinator: forced flush after kernel-change event, batch_size=1
```

carol sre: Cache telemetry: prefix cache hit ratio fell from 88% -> 42% on canary hosts, redis latency up. That would magnify compute costs per request.

dana pm: Any customer-facing errors reported? 504s, timeouts?

ev an cs: CS got a couple of escalation tickets. Acme Analytics reported slow UI and intermittent 504s on /api/generate during 15:02-15:12. BetaLabs reported degraded throughput in embedded search.

alice oncall: Immediate options: 1) flip batching-opt kill-switch, 2) revert kernel-affinity for canary hosts, 3) pause or rollback canary. Fastest is kill-switch.

bob runtime: Agreed. Flipping batching will stop the frequent small-batch flushes and reduce cache misses. Kernel-affinity revert is slightly slower (host commands + artifact consistency).

frank infra: I can scale the canary pool +12% to offset throughput loss from disabling batching if we go that route. Also investigating why some hosts didn't have the optimized kernel artifact available.

alice oncall: I'll toggle the flag for the canary scope now: `flagsctl set runtime:batching_optimized false --scope=canary-2026`

deploy-bot: flagsctl: runtime:batching_optimized=false (scope=canary-2026) applied by alice oncall at 1918012410.

carol sre: Watching metrics. p95 started to decline ~35s after flip. Cache hit% slowly increasing.

bob runtime: Good. Some hosts still log kernel fallbacks; looks like kernel-selection loop persisted on hosts with mismatched artifact sha. We should push host-affinity revert: `redwoodctl host set-affinity --scope=canary-2026 --affinity=stable-2025`

frank infra: Running affinity revert now and triggering artifact reconcile on hosts with bad sha. 10 hosts affected.

deploy-bot: redwoodctl: host affinity update queued by frank infra.

alice oncall: Customer impact estimate: roughly 6-8% of requests experienced >2x latency. Affected endpoints include /chat.stream, /embed.batch. CS notified. Dana, Evan prepare short external note but hold send until we see improvement.

ev an cs: Draft: "We've identified increased latency following a canary deployment and have applied mitigations. We're monitoring and will follow up with an incident summary."

dana pm: Good. We'll hold off on rollback for 30-45m if metrics show recovery.

carol sre: Affinity revert finished on 8/10 hosts. Kernel fallback logs have subsided on those hosts. Overall p99 down ~30% from peak.

bob runtime: Traces show batch flush events down ~75% and KV cache hit rate recovering. Remaining two hosts need manual artifact reconcile.

frank infra: I'm doing a manual redeploy of kernel artifact to the two stragglers. Also adding a pre-switch artifact validation step to the rollout pipeline.

alice oncall: We're seeing throughput dip ~10% with batching disabled, but combined with +12% pool scale that's within expected capacity. No new customer 5xxs in last 20m.

bob runtime: Proposal for next steps: 1) keep batching kill-switch off for canary while we reconcile kernel artifacts; 2) backfill kernel artifact and rerun canary after verifying artifact checksums; 3) patch batching coordinator to avoid immediate flush on kernel-change events (introduce a short debounce).

dana pm: Sounds safe. If we can get stable baseline in 45m, avoid full rollback. CS will send update to affected customers in 1hr.

alice oncall: Decision: flip kill-switch + apply kernel affinity revert + scale canary pool. Monitor 45m -> if stable, mark mitigated and require postmortem. If not, rollback canary. I'm handing post-incident ownership to @bob runtime for RCA; carol SRE remains backup.

bob runtime: Taking ownership. I'll capture traces/reproducer and start a postmortem draft. Preliminary root cause hypothesis: combination of experimental kernel affinity (missing optimized kernels on some hosts) + batching coordinator response to kernel-change causing batch-size collapse and cache thrash leading to high tail latency.

frank infra: I'll follow up with pipeline team to add artifact SHA validation gate and block affinity flips unless artifacts verified.

alice oncall: Mitigated -> customer impact contained. Opening postmortem ticket and assigning owners: bob runtime (root cause & fix), frank infra (deploy pipeline validation), carol sre (runbook update), dana pm & evan cs (customer comms).

evan cs: CS will follow up with the affected accounts tomorrow with a summary and actions. :white_check_mark:
